name: Isolated Left Ventricular Noncompaction Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Ratio of noncompacted to compacted myocardium > 2:1 at end-systole on echocardiography
Presence of deep intertrabecular recesses filled with blood from the ventricular cavity demonstrated by color Doppler
No coexisting congenital heart disease or other cardiomyopathies
Symptoms such as heart failure, arrhythmias, or thromboembolic events supportive but not required

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (trabeculation ratio > 2:1, deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow, and exclusion of other cardiomyopathies) must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Cardiac MRI criteria (Petersen criteria) may also be used for diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Identified on imaging as a hallmark feature

pathognomonic.symptomName: Deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow

common.notes: Due to systolic and/or diastolic dysfunction
Due to stagnant blood flow in recesses

rare.notes: Noncompaction affecting right ventricle is uncommon

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
Possible elevated troponin in myocardial injury
imaging: Echocardiography showing noncompacted to compacted myocardium ratio > 2:1
Color Doppler demonstrating blood flow in deep intertrabecular recesses
Cardiac MRI confirming extent of trabeculations and noncompaction
genetic: Mutations in sarcomeric and cytoskeletal genes (e.g., MYH7, ACTC1, TTN)
Familial inheritance patterns observed in some cases
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including ventricular arrhythmias and conduction delays

distinguishingFeatures: Diffuse ventricular dilation with systolic dysfunction
No deep intertrabecular recesses with blood flow

redFlags: Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope
references: Jenni R, Oechslin E, Schneider J, Attenhofer Jost C, Kaufmann PA. Echocardiographic and pathoanatomical characteristics of isolated left ventricular non-compaction: a step towards classification as a distinct cardiomyopathy. Heart. 2001;86(6):666-671.
Petersen SE, Selvanayagam JB, Wiesmann F, et al. Left ventricular non-compaction: insights from cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2005;46(1):101-105.
Towbin JA, Lorts A, Jefferies JL. Left ventricular non-compaction cardiomyopathy. Lancet. 2015;386(9995):813-825.
